segments.section: The object, the work and the movement have different histories
segments.text: The object, the work and the movement have different histories

segments.section: The object, the work and the movement have different histories
segments.text: The earlier-Teacher reconstruction proposes more than the survival of a sentence. It proposes that a founder's teaching, the community that preserved it, successor leadership and later biography have histories that can come apart and reconnect. The full transmission argument explains that ambition. A museum built from the research should let visitors inspect those different histories without turning one date on a wall label into a verdict about all of them.

segments.section: The object, the work and the movement have different histories
segments.text: A manuscript is a physical witness to a text at a stage in its transmission. A work can be copied, translated, excerpted or rearranged. An institution can preserve a work without descending from its first community. A community can inherit an office or practice without preserving every original text. These are distinctions within a possible historical connection, not reasons to reduce Micah's institutional hypothesis to harmless thematic similarity.

segments.section: The object, the work and the movement have different histories
segments.text: The strongest investigation asks which of those things is proposed to continue at each step and which evidence bears on that particular step. The source atlas makes the question explicit. Its catalogue separates works, material witnesses, translations, modern studies and author reconstructions, then gives each relationship a verb and a reason. "Survives in this copy" is different from "was composed here"; "quotes this work" is different from "descends from this community."

segments.section: A late copy can preserve an unexpectedly old work
segments.text: A late copy can preserve an unexpectedly old work

segments.section: A late copy can preserve an unexpectedly old work
segments.text: Cambridge's Artefacts of Ancient Judaism project highlights the Damascus Document as a work first encountered from the Cairo Genizah whose older counterpart emerged among the Dead Sea Scrolls. Its catalogue introduces the case as the first Dead Sea Scroll. This is a particularly useful example for the argument about a surviving witness: the antiquity of a work need not be limited to the date of the first copy modern scholars encounter.

segments.section: A late copy can preserve an unexpectedly old work
segments.text: The case supplies a methodological precedent, not the conclusion that any preferred early date is correct. The identification became more concrete because additional textual witnesses could be compared. A proposal about an earlier Thomas layer should therefore ask what comparison could perform equivalent evidentiary work: a distinctive reading, a traceable collection, a demonstrable quotation or a particular sequence of interpretation. The date of a late copy alone cannot answer the question of every earlier layer; the possibility of earlier

segments.section: A late copy can preserve an unexpectedly old work
segments.text: This principle applies to a skeptical response and to an encouraging one. A reply that says "the copy is late, therefore the earlier speaker is impossible" omits the transmission question. A reply that says "late copies can preserve early works, therefore this one preserves this Teacher" omits the identification question. The alternative reconstruction deserves development between those shortcuts, not replacement by either.

segments.section: Ethiopia is a history of reception, not merely a pin on a map
segments.text: Ethiopia is a history of reception, not merely a pin on a map

segments.section: Ethiopia is a history of reception, not merely a pin on a map
segments.text: The same Cambridge project presents Enoch through its preservation in full by the Ethiopian Church. The Library of Congress's 1993 exhibition separately describes an Aramaic Enoch witness, 4Q201, with a curatorial copying range around 200-150 BCE. That range belongs to a particular manuscript description, not to the complete Ethiopic corpus or every composition associated with Enoch.

segments.section: Ethiopia is a history of reception, not merely a pin on a map
segments.text: Together the cases make it reasonable to investigate a history wider than one discovery location or one language. They do not by themselves identify an uninterrupted chain from Zadokite priests to every community that later preserved Enoch. The relevant intermediate questions concern which texts circulated, their languages, who had access to them, and what could be learned about reception independently of a proposed ancestry.

segments.section: Ethiopia is a history of reception, not merely a pin on a map
segments.text: Micah's Egyptian and Ethiopian inquiry should retain its stronger institutional ambition while these questions are examined. A proposal that some people remained in Judea while others established a community elsewhere has a different structure from a claim that a book happened to survive in Egypt. It needs records of people and institutions as well as textual evidence. A museum should display the institutional path as a proposed path, not erase it because it has not yet been established and not render it indistinguishably from a documented

segments.section: Josephus demonstrates mediated evidence in plain sight
segments.text: Josephus demonstrates mediated evidence in plain sight

segments.section: Josephus demonstrates mediated evidence in plain sight
segments.text: Against Apion is useful both for what it says about an ancestral departure and for how the account reaches the reader. Josephus presents material attributed to Manetho and argues about its interpretation. A source relationship therefore runs from a quoted earlier account, through Josephus's presentation, to a later surviving text and modern translation. Each stage can preserve information while also introducing selection or framing.

segments.section: Josephus demonstrates mediated evidence in plain sight
segments.text: That gives the Hyksos-Exodus inquiry a precise question. What content is attributed to the earlier author, what interpretation belongs to Josephus, and what assumptions belong to a modern reconstruction? The answer should not be compressed into either "an Egyptian historian proved Exodus" or "a Jewish interpretation has no historical value." Both would bypass the actual transmission of the account.

segments.section: Josephus demonstrates mediated evidence in plain sight
segments.text: Antiquities 13.3 supplies another kind of evidence: a narrated Egyptian sanctuary associated with Onias. Its account is an institutional comparison target for Micah's displaced-priestly-community hypothesis. It does not, without additional arguments, specify the households left behind, identify John the Baptist with an earlier murdered priest, or establish the route to the Nag Hammadi texts. Those are particular links in the proposed reconstruction. They should be traced, not silently removed from its statement.

segments.section: Names can carry an office, a memory or an individual
segments.text: Names can carry an office, a memory or an individual

segments.section: Names can carry an office, a memory or an individual
segments.text: In the October Teacher discussion, Micah introduces succession, descendants and recurrent names to account for the movement's later participants. An objection that the same individuals would need to survive for more than a century does not address that formulation. The relevant questions concern how succession is documented, whether a designation refers to a name or office in each passage, and whether a later narrative represents a relationship differently.

segments.section: Names can carry an office, a memory or an individual
segments.text: Thomas's saying 12 directs attention to James; saying 13 distinguishes private instruction. They therefore give the investigation particular textual places to examine leadership and access to teaching, rather than only a modern preference for those subjects. Their functions do not automatically establish a Zadokite pedigree. But a response that refutes a pedigree inferred solely from an English synonym has not thereby answered a reconstruction based on naming, leadership, place, practice and historical continuity together.

segments.section: Names can carry an office, a memory or an individual
segments.text: The Melchizedek comparison is now available as a completed first passage study. It identifies several different grounds for priestly authority rather than treating every title as a family name. The next work is a fuller critical-text and historical-carrier comparison. The main transmission article has been corrected to link this completed first study instead of announcing that it still needs to be written.

segments.section: A museum can expose the argument rather than dramatize a verdict
segments.text: A museum can expose the argument rather than dramatize a verdict

segments.section: A museum can expose the argument rather than dramatize a verdict
segments.text: The future XR experience belongs to a separate implementation. This edition supplies content records for it, not rooms, navigation physics or a deployed headset application. Each proposed exhibit stop has a short label, the full argument behind the label, its source records, and the question a visitor should be able to investigate. Illustrations without verified reuse permission remain links, not downloadable textures disguised as cleared assets.

segments.section: A museum can expose the argument rather than dramatize a verdict
segments.text: The visitor should be able to distinguish a document's words from a scholar's reading and Micah's reconstruction. A proposal can be shown at full strength: an earlier founder, a successor community, a displaced biography, a competing chronology. Its display should also expose the evidence needed by a particular link. This makes a hypothesis inspectable without requiring a curator to normalize it into the dominant account before admitting it to the museum.

segments.section: A museum can expose the argument rather than dramatize a verdict
segments.text: That is also why a disagreement with an AI is recorded by outcome, not by applause. An objection that confuses copying with composition or ignores an explicitly stated mechanism can fail as an objection. That failure is a real argumentative result, but it is not a new manuscript. An unresolved identity question remains visible even when a particular dismissal is shown to be inadequate. The challenge record preserves those distinctions alongside the actual source turns.

segments.section: The book supplies the sequence; the atlas preserves its branches
segments.text: The book supplies the sequence; the atlas preserves its branches

segments.section: The book supplies the sequence; the atlas preserves its branches
segments.text: The book can lead from shared inheritance to contested teachers, inward interpretation, public authority and repair. The atlas allows a reader to pause that sequence and inspect an object, a passage, an alternative chronology or an answered objection. The museum can make those same branches spatial, with doors representing explained relationships rather than arbitrary proximity.

segments.section: The book supplies the sequence; the atlas preserves its branches
segments.text: The value is not a claim that every source has never appeared in another bibliography. It is the research configuration: what these sources are asked to explain together, which historical route is proposed, how the proposal changes when evidence is examined, and which debts make that inquiry possible. A shorter introduction should orient the reader inside that configuration, not replace its full argument.

segments.section: The book supplies the sequence; the atlas preserves its branches
segments.text: The first catalogue is deliberately bounded. Records labeled as leads are not represented as completed textual studies, and linking a work to a trail does not claim that its complete reception history has been reconstructed. The shared roadmap retains those tasks. What is already supplied is a connected route through evidence and reasoning that the book, wiki and future museum can use without maintaining three incompatible accounts.
